A2.text:
Leyla and her brother Orkhan walked in the beautiful forest near Gabala. Suddenly, Leyla heard a quiet noise behind a tree. She looked down and found a small, grey animal.

“Oh, look!” Leyla said with a big smile. “It is a stray puppy. He is so cold. Can we adopt him?”

Orkhan looked at the animal carefully. “I do not know, Leyla. He does not look like a normal dog. Look at his big ears.”

“But he is so cute,” Leyla answered. “I want to take him home to Baku. I can feed him and make him tame. He can be our domesticated pet.”

Orkhan shook his head. “We need to show him to a veterinarian first.”

They put the small animal in a box and drove to the animal clinic in the city. The doctor looked at the little grey animal and smiled.

“This is not a dog,” the doctor said. “You cannot keep him in an apartment.”

“What is he?” Leyla asked.

“He is a baby wolf,” the doctor answered. “He is a wild animal, not a pet. But do not worry. We will take him to a safe forest. That is his real home.”

Leyla laughed. “Well, I guess we need to buy a real dog next time!”

options: A girl finds a wild animal and wants to keep it
A brother and sister lose their pet dog
A doctor buys a new apartment in Baku
A wolf attacks a village in Gabala
questions.why: Leyla finds a baby wolf, thinking it is a stray puppy, and wants to adopt it as a pet.

questions.q: Where did Leyla find the small animal?
options: Behind a tree in the forest
questions.why: “Leyla heard a quiet noise behind a tree. She looked down and found a small, grey animal.”

questions.q: What did Orkhan want to do first?
options: Leave the animal in the forest
Show the animal to a veterinarian
questions.why: “We need to show him to a veterinarian first.”

questions.q: The doctor said Leyla could keep the animal in her apartment.
questions.why: The doctor said, “You cannot keep him in an apartment.”

questions.q: Leyla wants to make the animal “tame”. What does “tame” mean?
questions.why: She wants to feed it, make it tame, and keep it as a 'domesticated pet' in her home.

questions.q: How did Leyla feel at the end of the story?
options: She accepted she needed to get a real dog
She wanted to become a veterinarian
She was scared of the baby wolf
questions.why: She laughed and said, “Well, I guess we need to buy a real dog next time!”

B1.text:
Leyla and her older brother Orkhan were hiking in the beautiful forests of Gabala. While they were walking near a river, Leyla heard a quiet crying sound. She looked behind a large rock and found a small, grey animal shaking in the cold.

“Oh, look at this poor thing!” Leyla said. “It must be a stray puppy. He looks so hungry. Can we adopt him?”

Orkhan looked at the animal carefully. “Hold your horses, Leyla. Look at his thick fur and unusual eyes. That is the elephant in the room. He really does not look like a normal village dog.”

“But he is just a baby,” Leyla argued, holding the small creature in her jacket. “If we take him back to our flat in Baku, I am sure he will become tame. He can live a happy, domesticated life with us.”

Orkhan was not convinced. “We cannot just take strange animals home. Let's take him to a local veterinarian first to check if he is healthy.”

They drove into the town centre and visited the animal clinic. The doctor examined the little grey creature and immediately started to laugh.

“You definitely cannot keep this in a city apartment,” the doctor said.

“Why not?” Leyla asked in surprise. “Is he a dangerous predator?”

“He will be when he grows up,” the doctor smiled. “This is a baby wolf. In fact, this specific type of wolf is quite rare and slightly endangered in this area. His true habitat is high up in the mountains, not on a sofa in Baku.”

Leyla looked at the sleeping wolf cub and sighed. “Alright,” she said. “I suppose we will just get a normal dog instead!”

questions.q: What happens when Leyla tries to rescue a stray animal?
options: She learns how to train a hunting dog
The animal runs away before they reach the clinic
She discovers it is actually a wild baby wolf
questions.why: She wants to adopt a 'puppy', but the vet tells her it is a baby wolf.

questions.q: Why did Orkhan think the animal was not a normal dog?
options: It was making very loud noises
It had thick fur and unusual eyes
It tried to bite his hand
It was too big to fit in a jacket
questions.why: “Look at his thick fur and unusual eyes. That is the elephant in the room.”

questions.q: Where is the true home of the wolf cub?
options: Next to the river in the village
questions.why: “His true habitat is high up in the mountains, not on a sofa in Baku.”

questions.q: The brother and sister found the animal while swimming in the river.
questions.why: They were “hiking in the beautiful forests” and “walking near a river”, not swimming.

questions.q: Orkhan tells Leyla to “hold your horses”. What does this mean?
options: Put the animal on the ground
questions.why: He is telling her to slow down her plans of adopting the animal because it looks unusual.

questions.q: Why did the doctor laugh when he saw the animal?
options: The animal was doing a funny trick
Orkhan told a very good joke
Leyla brought a wild wolf to the clinic thinking it was a pet
The clinic was closed for the day
questions.why: He laughed right after examining it, realizing they brought a wild predator to the clinic hoping to keep it in an apartment.

B2.text:
Leyla and her brother Orkhan were spending their weekend hiking through the dense, autumn forests of Gabala. As they rested near a mountain stream, Leyla heard a faint, high-pitched whimper coming from a hollow log. She knelt down and gently pulled out a shivering, silver-grey creature.

“Oh, my goodness, look at this poor stray puppy,” Leyla cooed, wrapping her wool scarf around it. “He’s completely alone. We definitely have to adopt him and take him back to Baku.”

Orkhan crouched down and inspected the animal with a frown. “Hold your horses, Leyla. Let’s address the elephant in the room — look at the size of those paws, and his unusual golden eyes. That is not a normal village dog.”

“He is just a baby,” Leyla insisted, stroking the creature’s head. “With a little patience and training, I know he will become completely tame. We can give him a wonderful, domesticated life in our apartment.”

Orkhan sighed, knowing it was useless to argue when his sister made up her mind. “Fine, but we are taking him straight to a local veterinarian before we do anything else. We need to make sure he doesn't have any diseases.”

They carefully placed the sleeping animal in a cardboard box and drove into the town centre. When they reached the clinic, the vet took one look inside the box and burst into warm laughter, ready to let the cat out of the bag.

“Well, you certainly cannot keep this little guy in a city flat,” the vet chuckled.

“Why?” Leyla asked, looking confused. “Is he going to grow into an aggressive predator?”

“Exactly,” the vet nodded. “What you have found is a Caucasian wolf cub. They are actually becoming an endangered species in this specific region due to hunting. A wolf’s natural habitat is the high alpine forest, not a living room in the capital.”

Leyla stared at the fluffy cub, her dreams of city walks instantly fading. “I see,” she smiled a little sadly. “I suppose we should leave the wildlife in the wild, and look for a regular dog instead!”

questions.q: What is the main theme of the story?
options: The dangers of hiking alone in the autumn
How to properly treat a sick puppy
A misunderstanding about a rescued animal's true identity
questions.why: Leyla believes she is rescuing a stray dog, but discovers she has actually found a wild wolf cub.

questions.q: Where exactly did Leyla find the silver-grey creature?
questions.why: “Leyla heard a faint, high-pitched whimper coming from a hollow log.”

questions.q: Why are Caucasian wolves becoming rare in that region?
options: Because they are moving to the city
questions.why: “They are actually becoming an endangered species in this specific region due to hunting.”

questions.q: Orkhan successfully convinced Leyla to leave the animal in the forest.
questions.why: Orkhan did not convince her to leave it; instead, he sighed, “knowing it was useless to argue” and agreed to take it to the vet first.

questions.q: The vet was ready to “let the cat out of the bag”. What does this mean?
options: To let the animal escape into the room
questions.why: The vet was about to reveal the secret that the animal wasn't a dog, but a wolf.

questions.q: What does Orkhan's reaction to Leyla's stubbornness tell us about their relationship?
options: He knows her personality well and often gives in to her ideas
He completely ignores everything she says
He dislikes spending the weekend with her
questions.why: He sighed, “knowing it was useless to argue when his sister made up her mind”, showing he understands her stubborn nature.
